title: The Great Game of Business: Unlocking the Power and Profitability of Open-Book Management
author: Jack Stack with Bo Burlingham
core_themes: Transparency and trust in the workplace
primary_purpose: To demonstrate how businesses can achieve extraordinary growth and profitability by involving every employee in the financial workings of the company, teaching them how the business operates, and empowering them to act as owners.

structure_format.organization: Combines a chronological case study of Springfield Remanufacturing Corporation, practical step-by-step guidance, and actionable principles
features: Practical how-to guidance on open-book management
Key lessons summarized in each chapter

key_concepts_lessons: Open-book management means sharing key financial information with all employees, not just managers.
Teaching financial literacy gives employees the context to make informed decisions.
When employees participate in setting goals, measuring outcomes, and sharing profits, overall performance improves.
Creating a culture of ownership leads to higher accountability and engagement.
Small, regular ‘huddles’ keep everyone aligned with company goals.
Good business is like a game—everyone needs to know the rules, keep score, and have a stake in the outcome.
Trust and transparency are essential for sustainable business growth.
notable_features: Pioneering explanation and advocacy of open-book management
Draws on the real-life transformation of a company from the brink of bankruptcy to major success
Includes tools, checklists, and practical frameworks
Balances storytelling with actionable business methodology
cultural_historical_context: Published during a period of rising dissatisfaction with traditional hierarchical management and closed-door financials, the book helped spark a movement toward organizational transparency and participatory business models throughout the 1990s and beyond.
reception_impact: Widely hailed as a classic in business literature and management innovation
Credited with popularizing open-book management globally
Endorsed by business leaders for improving morale and profitability
Regularly used as a text in business schools and leadership training programs
